claim case No.502/2015 (Rajesh Prajapati Vs.
Dharmendra Patel and others)
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Off and on, the claimant was in hospital due to the crush injuries suffered by him in his left leg which was eventually amputated on 03.10.2012 but Tribunal has awarded Loss of Income only for a period of six months at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per month.
Similarly, meager amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head of Attendant and no amount is awarded under the head of Artificial limb which is required to be fixed.
Further, no amount is awarded under the head of Transport.
2. It is submitted by Shri Kapil Patwardhan, learned counsel for the claimant that Tribunal should have taken at least 80% disability while making calculation for Loss of Earning Capacity.
3 . Shri Rakesh Kumar Jain, learned counsel for the respondent No.3- Insurance company submits that impugned award is just and correct.

It is submitted that as per Schedule-I of Employees Compensation Act, 1923, doctor was required to certify the length of the stump and the place from where amputation was made so to bring it within the parameters of Entry 17 of Part 2 of Schedule I but Dr. Sharad Dwivedi who issued the Medical Certificate (Ex.P- 65) issued it on his own.

entities.text: Entry 17 of Part 2 of Schedule I
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
It is not a certificate issued by the District Medical Board and he has not mentioned the length of the stump left after the amputation and, therefore, the claimant having been failed to establish the length of the stump so to bring it within the parameters of Entry 17 in place of Entry 19, is not entitled to any escalation of percentage of disability.
4.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, first submission that disability should have been construed at 80% and not at 60% as has been construed by the learned Tribunal, is not made out.
Therefore, on this ground, no indulgence can be shown in the matter.

However, looking to the fact that claimant sustained crush injuries in the left leg in the accident and his left leg was eventually amputated on 03.10.2012 as is mentioned in para 19 of the impugned award, Loss of Income should have been awarded at least for one year.
Therefore, this amount under the head of Loss of Income is enhanced from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.60,000/-.
There will be addition of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Similarly, no amount is awarded under the head of Fixation of Artificial Limb, for which a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded.
Similarly, amount awarded under the head of Attendant is Rs.25,000/-.
Looking to the continuous care which was required by the claimant, this amount is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Thus, there will be enhancement of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Attendant.
No amount is awarded under the head of Transport.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under the head of Transport.

5. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.1,65,000/- (Rupees One Lakh, Sixty Five Thousands only) to which claimant will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
This additional amount will also earn interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
6. In above terms, this miscellaneous appeal is disposed of.
